```{python}
#| fig-alt: "Twenty small grayscale images of handwritten digits, in two rows and ten columns. Each column shows two examples of one digit, 0 to 9 from left to right, drawn as dark ink on a white background at 8 by 8 pixel resolution. The 0s are hollow ovals, the 1s are vertical strokes, the 3s are open on the left, and the 8s are closed on both sides."
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Row r of the file, read as an 8 by 8 grid, is image r.
images = pixels.reshape(-1, 8, 8)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 10, figsize=(8, 2))
for k in range(10):
    for row in range(2):
        ax = axes[row, k]
        ax.imshow(images[labels == k][row], cmap="gray_r", vmin=0, vmax=16)
        ax.set_xticks([])
        ax.set_yticks([])
    axes[0, k].set_title(str(k))
plt.show()
```

The first two images of each digit in the data.
